songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: Debut of The Other One, volcanic Garcia solos & soaring Lovelight
ai_show_review.blurb: The show bursts with high‑energy playing, highlighted by the first ever performance of "The Other One" and a searing Jerry solo. Pigpen’s organ on the suite and a radiant "Turn On Your Lovelight" keep the momentum rolling. Overall the set is tight, blues‑y, and pure 1967 psychedelia.
ai_show_review.review: Winterland on October 22 1967 captures the Grateful Dead at a pivotal moment – the band is locked in, firing on all cylinders, and they unveil "The Other One" for the first time. Jerry Garcia shreds with a volcanic lead that many reviewers call “brutal yet sweet,” while Phil Lesh lays down a tight counter‑point that drives the New Potato/Cryptical sections forward. Pigpen’s organ work on the suite is described as top‑notch, and his gritty vocals shine on "Turn On Your Lovelight" and "It Hurts Me Too." The rhythm section is rock solid: Bill Kreutzmann (Billy) holds down a one‑drummer groove that feels both propulsive and precise, while Mickey Hart adds subtle pliability in what appears to be his first recorded appearance. The set flows seamlessly from bluesy numbers like "Cold Rain And Snow" into extended jams, delivering an unforgettable snapshot of the band's early psychedelic era.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture – crisp, clean and amazingly clear for a 1967 source; no drop‑outs, fully captures the debut of "The Other One" and all key moments.

key_highlights: First performance of "The Other One" with a blistering Garcia solo
"Turn On Your Lovelight" shines with Pigpen’s organ and vocals
Tight interplay on New Potato Caboose / Cryptical Envelopment suite
Mickey Hart’s first recorded drum appearance adds subtle depth
song_highlights: Beat It On Down The Line

band_performance.Jerry: Blazing, volcanic lead on "The Other One" and high‑energy shredding throughout the set.
band_performance.Phil: Provides tight, melodic counterpoint; bass work shines especially during New Potato and Cryptical sections.
band_performance.Bob: Vocals stand out on "Beat It On Down The Line"; solid rhythm guitar support across the show.
band_performance.Pigpen: Organ work on the suite is top‑notch; vocal performances on Lovelight and Hurts Me Too are highlighted as great.
band_performance.Mickey: Makes his first recorded appearance, blending seamlessly with Bill for a pliable drum texture.
band_performance.Billy: Delivers solid, tight drumming in the one‑drummer (and later dual‑drummer) sections, keeping the high‑energy flow steady.

must_listen_sequences: Beat It On Down The Line
